Use these as hypotheses, not biographies. These are fictional composite personas synthesized from the supplied discovery references, MVP scope, and project-definition document. Names, quotes, devices, behaviors, and circumstances are illustrative. Validate them through separate interviews with students, household helpers, parents or guardians, project administrators, and PRC representatives before making irreversible product decisions.

Audience system

Persona matrix

The MVP has two primary users and three supporting actors. The beneficiary’s understanding and agency remain the central design test—even when another person initiates and pays for the membership.

Detailed profiles

The people the MVP must serve

BN

Bea Navarro

16 · Grade 11 student · Metro Manila · Student sponsor

Primary · Initiator

Bea wants to sponsor a Safe Card membership for the family’s longtime household helper. She is digitally confident, but she is still a minor and does not want the gesture to feel like charity, sales, or an instruction from an employer’s family.

DeviceMid-range Android phone
ConnectivityReliable Wi-Fi + prepaid LTE
LanguageEnglish / Tagalog
Digital confidenceHigh
“I want to help, but I need her to know this is her choice—not something she owes us.”Illustrative hypothesis; validate in research.

Job to be done

When I learn about Safe Card, help me explain and sponsor it responsibly so the beneficiary can decide freely and I can see whether my paid sponsorship was completed.

Goals

  • Understand the real benefits and limits before sharing.
  • Invite one known household helper respectfully.
  • Pay through an official PRC channel.
  • See only the status needed to help.
  • Keep a receipt and renewal date.

Barriers

  • Needs parent or guardian support for payment.
  • May unintentionally pressure someone employed by the family.
  • Does not know what information she may collect.
  • Loses confidence when PRC confirmation is slow.
  • Could mistake a referral count for verified membership.

What earns trust

  • PRC-approved, dated benefit content.
  • Clear distinction between invitation, agreement, payment, and activation.
  • Official payment destination and receipt.
  • Private, non-sensitive status updates.
  • Language that frames the act as support, not recruitment.

Safeguards

  • No personal data entered by the sponsor unless explicitly approved.
  • No automatic enrollment from payment alone.
  • No public beneficiary names or recipient leaderboard.
  • Parent/guardian or school rules applied where required.
  • Assisted registration only after beneficiary agreement.

MVP moments that matter

Landing page → plain-language benefit storyboard → private referral link or QR → beneficiary accepts invitation → external official-payment handoff → high-level status and receipt. Success means Bea can complete her tasks in under five minutes without seeing sensitive beneficiary data.

TR

Marites “Tess” Reyes

44 · Household helper · Tagalog/Cebuano speaker · Beneficiary

Primary · Decision-maker

Tess supports relatives outside Metro Manila and uses GCash and Messenger for familiar tasks. She is careful with links and forms, prefers straightforward Tagalog, and may use a shared phone. She wants time to understand the membership privately before agreeing.

DeviceEntry-level Android; sometimes shared
ConnectivityPrepaid, inconsistent LTE
LanguageTagalog; Cebuano/Bisaya
Digital confidenceLow to moderate
“Ipaliwanag muna sa akin kung ano ang kasama at hindi kasama. Ayokong pumirma nang hindi ko naiintindihan.”Illustrative hypothesis; validate in research.

Job to be done

When someone offers to sponsor me, help me verify that it is legitimate, understand the benefits and exclusions in my language, decide without pressure, and complete the official process without losing control of my information.

Goals

  • Know why the sponsor is offering the membership.
  • Understand the ₱1,200 annual fee and who pays it.
  • See benefits, exclusions, and claims deadlines.
  • Review and correct information before submission.
  • Keep membership proof and official support contacts.

Barriers

  • Fear of scams and fake PRC branding.
  • Long English copy and insurance terminology.
  • Limited time and mobile data.
  • Concern that saying “no” could affect work.
  • Uncertainty after submission or payment.

What earns trust

  • Tagalog first, with English and selected language options.
  • Visible PRC approval state and direct official contact route.
  • Short story-based benefit explanation with exclusions nearby.
  • Private agreement step and review screen.
  • Reference number, Safe Card ID, effective date, and claims instructions.

Safeguards

  • Payment is never represented as her consent.
  • She can pause, ask questions, decline, or resume later.
  • Sensitive details stay out of sponsor notifications.
  • Assisted entry happens only after agreement and in her presence.
  • Shared-device sessions protect or clear private information.

MVP moments that matter

Invitation → legitimacy check → benefits, limits, and claims education → informed agreement → three-minute mobile intake → review → submission confirmation. Success means Tess can explain the program’s purpose, cost, main benefits, and limits and knows to use Hotline 143 for accident-related ambulance or blood emergencies.

PN

Paolo Navarro

47 · Parent/guardian · Household employer · Payment supporter

Secondary · Safeguarding

Paolo supports Bea’s service project but wants assurance that money goes directly to PRC, that the household helper is not pressured, and that the family cannot see information they should not have.

DeviceiPhone + laptop
ConnectivityReliable home and mobile access
LanguageEnglish / Tagalog
Digital confidenceModerate to high
“Show me the official channel, the receipt, and how you make sure the offer is voluntary.”Illustrative hypothesis; validate in research.

Job to be done

When my child wants to sponsor a household helper, give me enough evidence to approve the payment and safeguarding approach without taking the beneficiary’s decision away from them.

Goals

  • Verify project and PRC legitimacy.
  • Understand total cost and refund process.
  • Confirm that the beneficiary chooses freely.
  • Use an official payment route.
  • Retain a receipt without receiving private beneficiary data.

Barriers

  • Unclear school rules for student-led fundraising.
  • Ambiguity between donation, membership, and insurance.
  • No defined dispute or refund path yet.
  • Concern about responsibility if a claim is denied.

Product implications

  • Provide a short sponsor/guardian explainer.
  • Show PRC approval and content review dates.
  • Separate payer details from beneficiary details.
  • Send payment evidence only to authorized parties.
  • State that PRC—not the school team—decides membership and claims.

Questions to validate

  • When must a parent or guardian approve?
  • Who is the legal payer and receipt holder?
  • What happens if the beneficiary declines after payment?
  • Which communications may include the student?
AM

Aira Mendoza

29 · School project administrator/adviser · First-line support

Operational · MVP admin

Aira supervises the pilot’s operations and authorized dashboard access. She must reconcile referrals, intake, and payment status, answer platform questions, maintain PRC-approved content, and escalate official program matters without attempting to resolve them herself.

DeviceLaptop + mobile phone
ConnectivitySchool/office broadband
ToolsSpreadsheets, email, admin dashboard
Digital confidenceHigh
“I need to know what is stuck, what I’m allowed to fix, and exactly when to hand it to PRC.”Illustrative hypothesis; validate in research.

Job to be done

When pilot cases arrive, help me see minimum necessary status, protect personal data, keep an audit trail, and route unresolved or official questions to PRC with complete context.

Goals

  • Monitor the funnel and identify “needs attention” cases.
  • Verify referral attribution and payment evidence.
  • Publish only approved content versions.
  • Export or hand off records in the PRC-approved format.
  • Produce aggregate pilot evidence.

Barriers

  • No final direct PRC integration for the MVP.
  • The backlog’s proposed pilot store conflicts with the decision that PRC stores all registration and payment data.
  • Manual reconciliation can create duplicate or stale records.
  • Support requests may mix platform, membership, payment, and claims issues.

Product implications

  • Protected role-based admin access.
  • Minimal fields, clear status ownership, and audit events.
  • PRC-controlled storage or approved transient handoff; synthetic data only until this is resolved.
  • Content approval record and rollback.
  • Aggregate reporting—not an advanced analytics suite.

Escalation boundary

  • Admin fixes navigation, form, or status-display issues.
  • PRC handles official eligibility, benefits, activation, payment disputes, and claims.
  • Privacy or safeguarding concerns follow the approved incident process.
  • No real data if the privacy gate is incomplete.
EC

Elena Cruz

38 · Philippine Red Cross liaison/approver · External authority

External · Approval owner

Elena represents the official program relationship. She reviews public copy and changes, confirms data and payment handoffs, and takes escalations that the project team cannot resolve. She needs a small, auditable approval workload—not scattered messages.

DeviceWork laptop + mobile
ConnectivityOffice and mobile access
ToolsEmail, document review, PRC systems
Digital confidenceModerate to high
“Give me the exact change, source, affected screens, and test evidence so I can approve it with confidence.”Illustrative hypothesis; validate with the assigned PRC liaison.

Job to be done

When the project team proposes content or workflow changes, give me an auditable package so I can approve, reject, or request revisions before anything goes live.

Goals

  • Protect the accuracy of Safe Card information.
  • Keep PRC systems as the source of truth.
  • Approve payment and data pathways.
  • Receive complete escalations with reference numbers.
  • Prevent the pilot from implying unauthorized PRC endorsement.

Barriers

  • Benefits and claims information may change.
  • Approval requests may lack source dates or impact details.
  • The MVP may use manual exports before integration.
  • Roles, response times, and backups remain to be named.

Product implications

  • Change log with content owner, source, review date, and approval state.
  • Preview or staging link for every public change.
  • Defined escalation categories and secure attachments.
  • Reconciliation report showing submitted, accepted, rejected, and corrected records.
  • Emergency rollback and visible version number.

Authority boundary

  • Only PRC confirms official membership, benefits, activation, and claims.
  • PRC approval is required before any production change.
  • Detailed exclusions and claims wording remain provisional until approved.
  • A backup approver and response target are still open decisions.

Scope reconciliation

What these personas should expect from Iteration 01

● Committed MVP

Mobile-first Tagalog/English landing page, plain-language benefit storyboard, referral QR/link, application-intake form, privacy notice and agreement checkpoint, PRC-controlled or formally approved transient data handling, protected admin access/export, confirmation and recovery states.

◆ Decision-gated

GCash or another payment integration, enrollee SMS/OTP, richer multilingual support, and direct verification depend on PRC approval, provider readiness, privacy decisions, and the final technical handoff.

○ Deferred

Direct PRC API integration, advanced analytics, public leaderboards, loyalty tiers or gamification, ambassador mobile app, location services, push notifications, multi-school automation, and national rollout.

Validation plan

Research questions before design sign-off

  • Student sponsors: What words make the invitation feel supportive rather than coercive or sales-driven?
  • Household helpers: Which language, examples, and proof points make the offer understandable and legitimate?
  • Consent: Can the beneficiary explain what data is collected, why, who receives it, and how to decline?
  • Assistance: When does assisted form completion help, and when does it make the beneficiary less comfortable?
  • Payment: Who pays in practice, what approval is needed for a minor sponsor, and what receipt is expected?
  • Status: What is the minimum sponsor-visible status that is useful without exposing private information?
  • Administration: Which cases can the project admin resolve, and which require immediate PRC escalation?
  • PRC approval: What evidence, owner, response time, and backup approver are required for each change?

Governance note

This is an internal discovery artifact, not PRC-approved public material. Every benefit, price, exclusion, claims instruction, translation, design using PRC identity, and production change requires PRC review before release. The linked journey map applies the same boundary.
